Christ Pantocrator

Icons

Christ

Christ Pantocrator

Christ Almighty · Pantokrator

What is depictedHistory and traditionPublished explanationSources

Scripture

John 1:14

Colossians 1:15

King James Version · Scripture previews

Christ Pantocrator presents Christ as the Almighty. Thomas Hopko’s explanation of church imagery places Christ the Almighty at the centre of the building, within a wider programme of images of the Church and Kingdom.

[1] Final paragraph: the canon of church design

What is depicted

The displayed Sinai icon shows Christ facing the viewer, with a cross-marked halo, a hand raised in blessing, and a richly covered Gospel book. It is a single frontal portrait rather than a narrative scene.

[2] Displayed work; file-page title and description

History and tradition

The image catalogue identifies this as the sixth-century encaustic Christ Pantocrator of Saint Catherine’s Monastery at Sinai. Its material and date belong to this particular surviving work, rather than to every later icon bearing the same title.

[2] Displayed work; file-page title and description

Published explanation

Hopko connects the possibility of depicting Christ with the Incarnation: the Word truly became human. His catechesis treats icons as witnesses to God’s presence and the Kingdom, with John 1:14 among its explicit scriptural foundations.

[1] Opening paragraph: the Incarnation and icons

And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth.

[3] John 1:14
